title: Exact Simultaneous Inference on Welfare Rankings in Two-Stage Experiments with Exact Quotas
banked_reason: TERMINAL:LAUNDERING — the delivered confidence-set kernel substitutes for the promised ranking-exponent and nonbalanced-allocation frontier; no honest bounded D0 repair exists.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish exact schedule inversion, a finite response-table quotient, and atomwise restrictions on deterministic weak-order confidence rules, but these are narrow finite-space inference results rather than the sharp ranking-exponent and allocation-frontier results advertised in the project brief.
No polynomial-factor upper or lower exponent, continuous fixed-allocation characterization, three-piece n=4 exponent, or nonbalanced optimizer is proved in the note.
No honest bounded same-topic repair: restoring fidelity requires the entire exponent/allocation theorem spine; solving oeq:consonant-order-closure only strengthens the substituted object.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a sound finite response-table inversion, an exact deterministic coverage characterization, and a sharp low-alpha order-atom obstruction. These results changed the paper's kernel: they did not prove the promised ranking-error exponents, matching least-favorable constructions, continuous allocation frontier, or explicit n=4 nonbalanced optimizer. Recovering the accepted topic would require rebuilding the full exponent/allocation theorem spine, while the remaining consonant-closure question only strengthens the substituted confidence-set problem.
tldr: Within the strict finite-population class of deterministic binary outcomes, equal cluster size, common interior exact quotas, exact first-stage arm totals, and uniform within-cluster quota subsets, the response-table inversion covers the complete causal welfare weak order with probability at least \(1-\alpha\). A proved finite population-indexed criterion exactly characterizes uniform coverage for any deterministic table-measurable order rule. Grouping compatible populations by their realized order defines a computable rational threshold \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\ge\delta_\star>0\); for \(0<\alpha<\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\), every uniformly valid rule contained in the baseline equals it at every compatible table. Whether that settled criterion can also be met by a lattice-consonant deterministic strict contained refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) remains open; randomized reporting is not covered.
gap: Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm construct simultaneous rank sets from valid simultaneous confidence regions for pairwise differences, while Rigdon and Hudgens invert exact tests for scalar interference effects. Bazylik, Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm obtain finite-sample rank sets only by exploiting a multinomial conditional law. None supplies an exact randomization-valid confidence set for the joint weak order of quota-policy welfares under fixed first-stage arm totals and within-cluster exact quotas.
fill: The core defines a max-discrepancy schedule-level randomization \(p\)-value, maximizes it over each weak-order fiber, and retains precisely the weak orders not rejected. The exact table law proves finite-sample simultaneous coverage, and the compression theorem supplies a finite algorithm whose operations are integer feasibility checks and rational table summation.
